name: Regulation & Licensing
description: Hong Kong has built one of the world's most comprehensive virtual asset regulatory frameworks. VATP licensing is mature, four new licensing regimes (dealers, custodians, advisors, asset managers) are advancing toward legislation, and the SFC continues to strengthen cybersecurity and investor protection requirements.
globalComparison: Regulatory breadth leads Singapore and Dubai — HK is building a full-spectrum VA licensing system; Dubai VARA has issued 51 licenses but with lower compliance thresholds.

description: VATP (Virtual Asset Trading Platform) licensing regime officially operational, requiring licensed operations
Stablecoin issuer regulatory framework officially came into effect
SFC/FSTB published consultation conclusions on VA dealer and custodian regulation
SFC/FSTB published consultation conclusions on VA advisory and asset management — four new licensing regimes taking shape
SFC mandated phishing-resistant authentication for VATPs, banning SMS OTP as sole login method
FSTB Secretary Christopher Hui confirmed the government will submit an amendment bill to LegCo within 2026 to establish a licensing regime for VA dealing, custody, advising and asset management

name: RWA / Tokenization
description: Hong Kong is a global leader in RWA tokenization: government directly participates in tokenized bond issuance, SFC approved the first native tokenized fund, and digital bond infrastructure (DACC) has landed in Hong Kong, marking a shift from government-led to market-driven diversification.
globalComparison: Globally leading — Hong Kong is the only jurisdiction with government tokenized bonds, SFC-approved tokenized fund, and dedicated clearing infrastructure simultaneously.

description: Hong Kong government issued the world's first tokenized green bonds, totaling HK$800 million
Project Ensemble moved from sandbox to EnsembleTX pilot phase, conducting real-value transactions
SFC approved the first real estate tokenization product and commodity RWA fund
Tokenized product secondary market opened to retail investors; Web3 Festival 2026 held
SFC approved Hong Kong's first fully native tokenized bond fund (Baillie Gifford), signaling global institutions accelerating Hong Kong expansion
DACC (Digital Asset Clearing Center) headquartered in Hong Kong, building infrastructure for tokenized bonds, stablecoins, and cross-border RMB settlement
FSTB announced a pilot to tokenize Exchange Fund Bills by end-2026, adding a new government-side RWA infrastructure initiative

name: Stablecoins
description: The stablecoin regulatory framework is fully operational: HSBC and Anchorpoint hold the first licenses, 36 formal applications are under review. As of early October the timing of a second batch remains market speculation — the HKMA has declined to comment and issued no official confirmation.
globalComparison: Framework maturity comparable to Singapore's MAS framework, but with a distinct large-bank-focused licensing strategy; mainland China's Circular 42 explicitly banned unauthorized yuan stablecoins.

description: Stablecoin Ordinance officially came into effect; HKMA became the stablecoin issuer regulator
HKMA received 36 formal stablecoin issuer license applications
Mainland China issued Circular 42, banning unauthorized yuan stablecoins and asset tokenization
First licenses granted: HSBC (HKD stablecoin, integrated with PayMe) and Anchorpoint Financial (Standard Chartered × Animoca Brands)
HKMA relaxed compliance requirements for licensed stablecoin issuers, lowering barriers to entry
HKMA says 'open yet cautious' on more licenses; market rumors suggest second batch may be approved around October National Day
HKMA declined to comment on rumors of a second licence batch around October; timing remains unconfirmed ('36 to 2' still speculation)
